Vicor Expands Capacity as Fab-1 Nears Limit
Vicor is acquiring a 334,000-square-foot building on 66 acres in Merrimack, New Hampshire, plus 54 acres in Hooksett.
The sites will support ChiP Fab-2 and Fab-3, with a combined footprint of nearly one million square feet.
The expansion will add capacity beyond Vicor’s 320,000-square-foot ChiP Fab-1 in Andover, Massachusetts, which is nearing full utilization. ChiP Fab-2 has a one-year lead time to initial deployment.
Vicor entered the expansion with a growing backlog. Second-quarter backlog reached $380 million, up 26% sequentially and 145% from a year earlier.
Cash and cash equivalents increased 12.2% sequentially to about $453.6 million as of June 30.
Expansion Targets AI Demand
Vicor said the added capacity will help support OEMs and hyperscalers while increasing U.S.-based sourcing.
The company said its Vertical Power Delivery technology is designed for advanced AI applications constrained by multi-phase and integrated voltage regulators.
Vicor expects its licensing model and broader ChiP fab network to improve supply predictability for the AI hardware ecosystem.
The expansion comes as power infrastructure emerges as a key constraint on AI data-center growth.

What Vicor Does

Vicor develops modular components and systems for converting and managing electrical power. Its portfolio includes power converters, integrated circuits, filters, input modules and configurable power systems.
